title: Meeting Cozy Cole, Les Paul and Charlie Christian
summary: On his third night he heard Cozy Cole at a club on 142nd Street and played behind Les Paul and Charlie Christian.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: And then, like the third night, that was the first time I ran in to Cozy Cole. There was a club at 142nd Street, and 7th Avenue -- oh my God, I can't remember, right down the street from the Woodside Hotel. The guy that had the group, and it was Freddie Moore; Freddie Moore, the drummer. Freddie Moore had the group in there --
142nd Street and 7th Avenue, right on the corner.
Gee, I can't recall it either.

Yeah, well, anyway, that's the first time I ran in to Cozy Cole. Cozy Cole, Charlie Christian and [Fred Rand] was in town, and a guitar player that was with him that first started the multiple sounds on the recording --
Yeah, his name was Les Paul, remember him?
Yeah, that was the first time I heard him and Charlie Christian; they hooked up together that night, because I played the drums behind them.
So that was my first time running into Cozy Cole, too. Man, I was looking at this cat with my mouth open, I had heard so much about Cozy Cole when I was in Florida.
